mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen 6.8 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w despite sustained workplace suppression. This upward trend in retail mobility, if it continues at the observed rate of ~2.3 points per week, will produce higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks than the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose from -20.1 to -13.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the mean of the last 28 days (-16.75).

mechanism_narrative: Grocery and pharmacy mobility has stabilized near baseline (0.7 at t-0w), signaling consumer confidence in essential-goods access. This confidence spillover reduces precautionary behavior and increases discretionary retail visits, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose from -1.0 to 0.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or remains flat over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining at or above 0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved by 7.3 points from t-3w to t-0w, indicating increased commuting and public movement. When transit access improves, retail-district accessibility increases, enabling higher retail-and-recreation visits over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next four weeks despite TRANSIT continuing to improve by more than 5 points per week.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has declined sharply in t-1w (-21.9) before recovering to -10.9 in t-0w, consistent with seasonal weather volatility in mid-December. This outdoor-activity suppression redirects discretionary mobility indoors to retail venues, increasing RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -10.9 in t-0w after dip to -21.9
failure_condition: PARKS mobility recovers above -5 and RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 8.1 to 5.1 over four weeks, indicating reduced home-confinement behavior. Combined with rising RETAIL_REC trend, this signals a shift toward out-of-home activity. The interaction of declining residential time and rising retail access will accelerate RETAIL_REC gains over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while RETAIL_REC rises simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell 3.0 points while RETAIL_REC rose 6.8 points
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL continues to decline but RETAIL_REC does not increase over the next four weeks, or RESIDENTIAL reverses upward.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES remain suppressed at -19.1 in t-0w with minimal improvement over four weeks. Sustained workplace closure signals ongoing restrictions. Under such restrictions, retail mobility is capped; if restrictions persist unchanged, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed or decline further over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains below -18 for four consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -19.1 in both t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -15 within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases despite sustained workplace suppression below -18.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES show weak co-movement (both suppressed but stable). When transit and workplace mobility are both constrained, retail access via public transport is limited, suppressing RETAIL_REC. If both remain suppressed over the next four weeks, RETAIL_REC will decline or stagnate.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -45 AND WORKPLACES below -18 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -46.3 and WORKPLACES at -19.1 in t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rises above their respective thresholds, or RETAIL_REC increases despite both remaining suppressed.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS suppression at -10.9 in t-0w combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM near zero indicates consumers are prioritizing essential trips over discretionary outdoor activity. This behavioral shift toward necessity-driven mobility will constrain discretionary retail visits, causing RETAIL_REC to decline or plateau over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS below -10 AND GROCERY_PHARM within -1 to +1
failure_condition: PARKS recovers above -5 or GROCERY_PHARM rises above 2, and RETAIL_REC increases over the next two weeks.
